newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher, supported by pessimism on economy.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher, supported by pessimism on economy.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was higher by midday on Monday, supported by the market's pessimism about the economy and the Finance Ministry's outright bond buying, traders said.
"Short-covering has been predominant since the release of (April) industrial output data last week, and today we are seeing a continuation of such short-covering," a brokerage house trader said.
Due to the market's increased sensitivity toward economic fundamentals, there will be some focus on the May domestic vehicle sales data due at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT), traders said.
The June stood at 124.26 by midday, up from Friday's close of 124.01. Turnover was 32,435 contracts.
The key 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.505 percent as of 0217 GMT, down from Friday's close of 2.535 percent.
MOF's Trust Fund Bureau offered to buy 100 billion yen in bonds outright in an agreement starting on June 5, the Bank of Japan said on Monday.

Although the market showed little reaction after the outright bond buying took place, JGBs rose earlier, based on speculation that MOF would buy bonds outright this morning, the brokerage house trader said.
Some traders said talk that May domestic vechicle sales figures would come in weaker than expected may also have triggered buying.

"The market's initial expectation was for the May vehicles sales data to come in at around minus 10 percent year-on-year, but there has been some talk that the figures may turn out lower than that," a foreign bank trader said.
Dealers are buying back, fearful that the market will begin focusing more on the weak economic fundamentals, he said.
The market is now focusing on whether investors will soon start actively buying cash JGBs, traders said.
There was talk that firmness of the benchmark 182nd JGB and other long-term JGBs was due to the unwinding of short basis positions, the brokerage house said.
Unwinding a short basis position involves buying cash JGBs and selling JGB futures.
Activity was dominated by dealers this morning, and investors were relatively inactive, the brokerage house trader said.
The JGB market may begin testing the upside in the near term based on its pessimistic view on the economy, a trader for a long-term credit bank said.
"The market's next target, with regard to the 182nd cash JGB is likely to be 2.4 percent," the trader said.

Although the market now feels that the economy's slowdown over the April-June period will be weaker than initially expected, there is still concern about a possible interest rate rise in the future, the brokerage house trader said.
Against such a backdrop, JGBs are likely to be range-bound until the release of the key "tankan" survey on June 25, he said.
